XOR bit mask $08 into $0504, $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 11 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $10 into $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 12 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $20 into $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 13 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $40 into $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 14 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $80 into $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 15 crosses the X boundary.
Wait briefly, then shift screen codes and color nybbles left by one cell using straight-line copies of the rows. Code from $150C through $1C84 performs the row copies with Y indexing.
Continuation of the screen and color RAM shift. This middle group continues the unrolled cell copies across the $42xx/$DAxx pages before passing to the $43xx/$DBxx group.

Walk 22 row records from $BC70. Each stores a stream pointer and a count, advanced by this routine as it emits the next rightmost screen code. Select a color nybble from the table at ($69) and write it to the corresponding color RAM cell.
Operand of AND at $1D32. The right-column routine changes it based on camera X before writing the emitted cell.
When $86 is set and the high byte of camera X equals $10, set $85 to $FF.
Initialize 22 row cursors from the selected length-prefixed streams and seed each repeat counter with $FF. Then look up the round's object event stream in $C300.

Select the round's compressed row data using $6B. Initialize 22 row cursors, skipping from the beginning of each row to the camera's starting cell for a nonzero position. Also seek the five-byte event stream to the restart threshold.
Four little-endian pointers to row streams at $8000, $9090, $9749 and $9CE7. Indexed by the zero-based round at $6B.
High bytes of the four round-layout addresses interleaved with their low bytes at $1EC1.

Initialize vitality and background, select round data, and decode the first right column. Build a visible starting field by requesting forty character shifts, then set the area and round digits and initialize per-attempt state.
Set the interrupt mask, load A, X and Y from $4B, $4C and $4D, clear the mask and return. The round initialization path immediately before it jumps to $3E40.

Process five-byte event records before camera X plus $0140. Advance the cursor, require the event area mask to match $6C, and initialize an available actor. Read its type flags and call its initializer through the word table at $20CA.
Jump indirectly through the vector at $0780, set by the event spawner before its JSR here.
Choose $052A when the first slot's status is zero. Otherwise check twelve 16-byte slots from $056A for zero at offset $0C. On success, leave the record pointer in $57/$58 and return zero.
Clear offset $0C in each of the sixteen 16-byte actor records beginning at $052A.
Fill screen matrix bytes $4078 through $43FF with $A0, preserving the first three rows.
Set the active bit at offset $0C of the actor when its X coordinate is on the same page within $50 units to the right of the player.
Subtract player X from the actor X field pointed to by $57 and return the low byte in X and the high byte in A.
Word addresses for the spawn initializers. This portion starts with the shared $21EE initialization path.
The spawner reads the high byte of initializer addresses from this indexed base. The paired low byte is at $20CA.
High byte of the actor initializer table word whose low byte is at $210A.
Remaining dispatch words for object types $21 through $91, including the seven boss types $77–$7D that share $23F2.
Copy the two saved palette entries at $062F/$0630 to $4F/$50 and clear bits two and three of the player actor's flags.
Write one to the actor's horizontal speed field.
Return after writing actor field nine through the store at $2205.
Set vertical speed to two with field nine set to $10. Save $5D and $B5 as the two actor limits.
Set signed vertical speed to minus one and field nine to $0C. Store limits $8A and $B5 in fields 13 and 14.
Return after the actor field store at $2233.
Set field nine to eight and signed vertical speed to $DF. Store limits $9A and $B5 in fields 13 and 14.
Return after the actor model parameter store at $224A.
Supply Y limits $6A and $AA to the shared initializer at $2263.
Supply Y limits $7A and $9A to the shared initializer at $2263.
Supply Y limits $8A and $B5 to the shared initializer at $2263.
Set the lower and upper limit bytes to $5D and $9A and initialize vertical speed to one through $2263.
Write signed $FE to actor field ten.
Return after writing the initial vertical speed at $2276.
Write $20 to field nine and signed $FC to field ten.
Return after writing the initial actor field at $2282.
Supply $72 to the shared actor field-eight store at $2293.
Supply $6B to the shared actor field-eight store at $2293.
Supply $45 to the shared actor field-eight store at $2293.
Supply $46 to the shared actor field-eight store at $2293.
Return from the shared actor field-eight store.
Release the actor slot if the existing axe flag at $0631 is nonzero.
Write ten to the actor's horizontal speed field nine.
Return after writing the actor's initial horizontal speed at $22A5.
Supply $1E to the shared vertical speed store and request sound selector seven.
Set vertical speed to $32 and request sound selector seven.
Set $064A and join the shared actor initializer with A=$FF.
Set $FB and actor field eight to $FF, clear bit three of field 12, and seed fields nine and ten with $20 and eight.
Set actor field ten to $E7, or $DF if the area mask overlaps $60.
Return after the actor field store at $22E7.
Set actor field ten to eight through the shared store at $22EC.
Supply signed vertical speed minus eight to the shared store at $22EC.
Run the common initializer at $22EA and store limits $6A and $B5 in actor fields 13 and 14.
Set actor field nine to $10 and record paired X positions $50 either side of the spawn X in fields 6–7 and 13–14.
Return after the actor initializer writes its final field at $2329.
Choose signed velocity $F8, or $F0 when the area mask overlaps $60, and continue to the common field-ten store.
Walk object records and call the type-specific conversion path for food types $61, $63, $65 and $67. Preserve the caller's actor pointer across the scan.
With $0660 set, select type $91. Continue at the common parameter initialization at $23AD.
Under $0649, change the actor type to $62 and use the parameter pair $02/$6F. Otherwise use the parameter pair at $23C0.
If $0649 is set, change the type to $64 and continue to the parameter pair at $23AD. Otherwise continue at $23D3.
Supply $02 and $6F as the pair written to fields 13 and 14 by $23D7.
If $0649 is set, change the actor type to $66. Otherwise pass $50 and $6D as the field 13 and 14 parameters to $23D7.
If $0649 is set, change the type to $68 and continue at $23AD. Otherwise write parameter pair $01/$6E to fields 13 and 14 and initialize field eight to $C8.
Return after storing the second parameter of the selected actor variant.
Request music selector $19 and release this actor slot.
Request music selector $16 and release this actor slot.

Clear $066A, then select the shot interval and hit target from the first set area bit. Save the parent pointer and allocate six attached parts by copying the parent record and adjusting their positions and types.
Copy the saved actor pointer from $2A/$2B back to $57/$58.
Reserve a slot, copy all 16 fields of the parent actor and move the copy down by $15. Set its type to $8E and continue at $247C.

Remove the prospective actor if the HUD counter has reached eight or $90 is already nonzero. Otherwise advance the generator at $24E9 and compare its result with the current area's threshold at $24CF. Set $90 when the result is below the threshold.
Area-indexed cutoff values for the extra actor spawn test at $24C2. The candidate is accepted only when the generated byte is below the cutoff.
Signed Y offsets indexed by the six attached boss-part entry points and added to the parent actor Y.
Read with the boss-part index at $2472 and written to field five of the allocated actor.
One delay for each of seven areas. Boss initialization uses the lowest set area bit as its zero-based index and seeds both the reload and running timers.
Add $FA and $76 to the previous byte at $91, retaining the incoming carry for the first addition. Save the result at $91 and return it in X.

Scan five keyboard controls with the CIA mask pairs at $2538. Combine their active-low results with the port 2 joystick from $DC00. Compare bits 4 and 0 to the previous poll and latch new fire and jump presses.
Five pairs traversed backwards by $24F3. The first byte selects columns on CIA1 port A and the second masks the reading from port B.
Second bytes of the pairs at $2538. The poll uses these masks on CIA1 port B for the corresponding keyboard controls.
Select a keyboard column using the table at $BBF0 indexed by X and return the port B bits selected by the mask at $BC30.

Predict the player's next Y, clamp it to the field, and classify three cells beneath the player. Glyph codes after OR with $80 map to three classes divided at $90 and $E0. The returned base-three case routes the floor handling.
Convert the camera-relative X and prospective Y to a matrix position. Inspect a column of up to four cells and clear vertical motion on the obstructed path.
Subtract camera world X from player world X. For a nonnegative difference, divide the difference by two, add two, divide by four and add three to form the screen-column argument for $25EF.

Compute the actor's camera-relative screen column and prospective collision row. Classify the three terrain cells into three ranges split at $90 and $E0. A position behind the camera uses a separate result path.
Multiply A by X with an eight-step shift-and-add loop, returning the unsigned product in $42/$43.
During downward motion, scan actor records with the active and platform flags. Test horizontal and vertical overlap, then place the player above a matching actor and reset vertical displacement.
Reject the test during an existing gameplay outcome. Compare actor and player coordinates to a finite horizontal distance and an asymmetric vertical window, returning $FF for overlap.
Test the two projectile slots at offsets $20 and $30. Require an active slot and overlapping X and Y, then return $FF for a collision or zero if neither passes.
Shift A right three times, explicitly setting carry from the current sign before each rotate. Negative values round down.

Clear per-update jump and fire edges and advance the player pose counter. Every four phases replace eight bytes of a character shape staging table. A nonzero outcome selects the path that initializes and animates the loss state.
Double the actor type from A, read the target word from $35EA and jump indirectly through $0784/$0785.
If $066B is zero, copy the saved type from $066C to the player record and resume movement-state selection. Otherwise decrement the countdown and enter the same selection code.
Return while the round flag is negative. When a boss round is finishing, check the player position and completion gate, then either use the normal control poll or a scripted rightward input.

Poll the joystick and keyboard, invert to active-high, choose horizontal and jump constants, and run object-platform and terrain handling. The terrain path ultimately dispatches by the surface code from $2551.
Set $66, decrease vertical speed by two and run the player movement calculations. Once the velocity is negative and Y reaches $FA, set $0632.
Apply the same gravity and movement as $2A55. Select pose zero while velocity is nonnegative and pose two while negative, and set $0632 when falling reaches Y=$FA.
Subtract two from the signed vertical speed at $0534 and use $81 for a negative overflow.
Set $66 and $21, subtract $7E from the player's vertical speed with the $81 negative-overflow limit, then continue at $2B26.
Read the middle terrain sample and choose one of fourteen height-profile entries based on camera-relative X phase. A code outside that range enters the common platform motion path.
Set the common motion constant to eight. Account for the jump edge and the current control-derived jump value before selecting the standing pose and movement branch.
Apply vertical motion to the player at actor offset zero, then to the attached platform object if $78 selects one.
Derive the rolling pose and target speed from the left control and motion state before applying movement. The routine keeps a nonzero speed when braking on this path.
Derive horizontal fractional state from the actor's velocity field. Use the signed vertical value to compute a candidate Y, with a cell-boundary correction when the collision branch requires it.
On a new fire press with the axe state set, use the first of two available projectile slots. Seed it from the player's position and facing, then request the throwing pose when movement state permits.
Fourteen vertical adjustments selected by the middle floor tile when bit 2 of camera-relative X is clear.
Fourteen vertical adjustments used when bit 2 of camera-relative X is set.
Clamp A to the signed range -63 through +63. The entry branches on the incoming N flag, which must describe the sign of A.
Two groups of eight sprite-cell pointers. The animation path at $28A4 copies the selected group into the player sprite staging buffer.

Advance the animation counter every fourth pass, scan the active actor records, and dispatch object updates through $35EA when their status permits. Actors that still await activation pass through $20A6.
Jump indirectly through the per-type handler vector at $0782.
Test for an axe hit, run the common actor adjustment and toggle field 12 bit zero. On alternate calls subtract four from world X and add one to Y, capped at $B5.
The idle actor waits until it is within $5A units to the right of the player, then moves and switches phase at Y $9A. Axe contact enters the common hit handler with selector $29.
On player overlap use the special replacement path when $064A is set and the protection-consumption path when $84 is set. Otherwise write outcome $0C.
Choose protection consumption when $84 is set, or proceed to write outcome $0C.
Write gameplay outcome $0C when contact reaches the unprotected path.

Compare the actor age plus one with $10. At or above the threshold replace its type with the current area's entry from $370E and leave the old age in place. Below it, save the new age and update animation at $2F58.
Advance the introductory animation to age $10. In area mask $40 and round index three, remove the actor if the camera high byte has reached $10. Otherwise use the transformation at $2F44.
Release the actor when the camera high byte has reached $10.
Replace the current actor with type $6E, seed field eight to $20, and pass the X=$01 score argument to $F652.
Store the updated age and select an animation frame by dividing it by four.
Test hits from either axe. On player contact copy the player's speed and facing into the egg actor, set its vertical motion and switch its type to $3A, the moving egg or contents path.

While the terrain case indicates a fall, adjust vertical motion and remove the actor if it drops past $E8. When placed on the terrain, restore the actor's intended type and run that type's initializer. Types $72 and $6B substitute $3D when the player lacks the axe.
One-byte return entry immediately before the rebound handler.
Supply rebound velocity $3A before entering the shared update at $2FEC.
Set $063C to $46 and enter the shared bouncing actor update.

Save the rebound velocity from A. Reduce signed Y velocity by two with an $81 overflow limit and move vertically. From Y=$F0, replace the velocity with the saved value and request sound seven. An axe hit replaces this actor with type $42.
Run the common actor adjustment and check whether an axe overlaps. On a hit consume the axe and change the actor to type $44 via the score path.
Activate the motion state near the player. Advance falling motion when its terrain case is $0D and replace it with type $48 on the other terrain or hit path.
Release the actor if the sign bit of field eight is already set. Otherwise subtract one from that field.
When field eight is zero, clear the flags in field 12. Otherwise decrement the countdown.
Only player contact proceeds to set $0649 and update the food records.
Set $0649 and update the existing food actor records, then release the current slot.
Write zero to field 12 to clear the actor's active flags. Round initialization temporarily changes the entry opcode to RTS.
Decrement field eight and use the result XOR three as the frame value. When field eight is already zero, clear field 12.
On player overlap release the slot and set the axe-equipment flag at $0631.

Remove the actor when the terrain classifier returns a case other than $0D. Otherwise subtract two from its vertical speed, count field nine down to zero and move vertically. Remove it once Y reaches $EE.

While $064A is negative, an update with a nonzero timer decrements it and follows the player. An update starting at zero sets $064A to $7F and skips following. The departing actor is released after leaving the permitted vertical range.
With $FB negative, position the effect relative to the player. Otherwise apply vertical motion and remove the actor outside $1E through $E5, clearing $FB when it leaves.
Set the actor X to player world X minus $10 and actor Y to player Y minus $15. Interrupts are disabled while reading and copying the player position.
Integrate Y and replace values less than eight with $FC.
Integrate Y and replace values at least $F8 with four.
Move vertically and choose the Y threshold from field 13 or 14 by the sign of the velocity. Reverse velocity and move back once the corresponding limit is crossed.
Move the actor by one X unit, using status bit 3 for its direction. On reaching the camera or its stored bounds, flip the direction bit instead of committing a further step.
If field eight is nonzero, apply vertical movement. Release the slot if the resulting Y is less than $0A.
Choose between object types $23 and $24 from the terrain case. Drive its motion and count accepted axe contacts. The first changes the motion and the second enters hit handling with type $25.
Subtract four from actor field ten and store the result with the $81 overflow limit. Select animation frame two if the unbounded result had its sign bit set, otherwise zero.
Clear the two velocity fields and measure horizontal distance from the player. If the actor is on the forward, same-high-byte side and the low difference is less than $5A, seed speeds $18 and $3C.
Store $18 in actor field nine and $3C in field ten.
On axe contact consume the axe and set the actor type to $8F. Continue to the player-overlap handler.
Consume an overlapping axe and replace the actor with type $27 via the score path. Without an axe hit, continue to the player-overlap handler.

On player overlap take the score argument from field 13 and the replacement actor type from field 14. Start the $20 count, play sound $0B and update vitality and the score. Otherwise count down field eight and switch to type $75 when it expires.
On player overlap request sound $0B, set $0660 and release the actor slot.
When the player touches the actor, request sound $0B and set the vitality pair to $60F8 with interrupts disabled, then release the slot.
On player overlap request sound $0B, increment the count at $0653, redraw the marker row and release the actor.
On player overlap set $8E to nine and set the protection flag $84 before removing the pickup.
On overlap clear $85 and $86, request sound $0B and remove the pickup.
If boss status at $0654 is zero, set bit six of actor field 12.

Deflect an overlapping axe. Process player overlap only when the cooldown is zero. Branch to the special handling for $064A or $84 if set, otherwise prime the cooldown to eight and subtract six vitality units with a floor at zero.
Branch to contact vitality loss when protection is clear. Otherwise consume protection.
Set the damage cooldown to eight and subtract six from the vitality high byte. Clamp a borrow to zero.
Run the common contact handler and check for an axe hit. On a hit consume the axe and use type $1F as the replacement.
Test player overlap and branch to the replacement or damage path according to $064A and $84.
Without $84 protection, set outcome $0B and request sound $17. Otherwise set $8E, clear the protection flag and change the actor to type $34 through $35AB.
Run the shared adjustment and toggle field 12 bit zero. Integrate horizontal speed on the set phase. On an axe hit replace the actor with type $1D and award the hit score.
Test player overlap and handle contact before integrating horizontal speed. On an axe hit replace the actor with type $3F through the hit reward path.
Set outcome $0C on player overlap. Choose vertical velocity $28 on terrain contact or apply gravity in terrain case $0D, move the actor, and remove it at Y=$E6 or below.
Wait for the player to approach within $50 horizontal units, then update the actor until Y reaches $B5 and switch phase. The hit path uses effect type $30.
Apply gravity in increments of four with the $81 overflow limit and integrate the vertical position. Remove the actor at Y=$E6 or below.
Select movement parameter $22 and join the shared vertical limits routine.

Subtract the actor's signed vertical velocity, compare the new Y against the stored limit for that direction and reverse on the bound. Advance horizontal motion and use the common hit routine on axe contact.
Scale the unsigned speed at actor offset 9 into a fixed-point delta. Add or subtract it from actor X and the fractional byte at offset $0F, according to the direction bit at offset $0C.
Apply the horizontal step, then continue into the signed vertical step.
Pass signed velocity from field ten through the scaling routine at $286A. Subtract the resulting displacement from field two, the actor Y coordinate.
Replace actor field ten with its two's-complement negation.
Store the replacement type in A, clear bit three of field 12, send the X=$30 score argument and continue at $32DA.
Replace the actor with type $34, zero field eight and request sound selector one.
Run the axe overlap test. On contact, clear the colliding projectile's actor status, request sound 6 and return $FF.
Run the axe overlap test. On contact, set the projectile's direction bit, halve its horizontal speed, request sound $0A and return $FF.
146 little-endian update handlers, addressed by twice the actor type in $2DDB. Shared pointers route multiple types into the same update.
The actor update loop reads each handler's high address byte here at the same offset as its low byte at $35EA.
High byte of the actor update table word whose low byte is at $362A.
Remaining per-type update words beginning with type $21. Types $77–$7D share the main boss handler.
Actor types selected by the current area's first set bit when the age counter at $2F01 reaches $10.

Collect actors with the relevant status bits and Y below $F0. Sort by Y when more than eight qualify, discard actors off the left edge, and prepare camera-relative positions and per-sprite flags for the raster handlers.
Map a sprite-list index modulo eight to a hardware register writer from $C01E and save the mask from $3933 alongside it.
Per-position bitmask for retaining X high and expansion bits from the first render group.
Per-position bitmask selecting the second render group's replacement X high and expansion bits.
Map the number of recycled sprites to the bit pattern stored for a reload stage at $391F.

Dispatch according to the boss phase. During the active fight, update side-to-side movement and its shot timer, count accepted axe hits and change the phase at the area-specific hit threshold. The defeated path moves a component downwards, then changes the boss actor into its post-fight state.
Use area-dependent pacing and bounce the boss between X $1050 and $10D0. Under the shot timer and hit flash tests, spawn type $84 and count a new hit only after the flash gate allows it.

Test for contact with a hit source when the boss hit cooldown is clear. Start a 12-tick flash and count the hit. At the end of the cooldown, compare the total to the area target and enter the defeated phase if reached.
Select boss Y-displacement index zero. If $0654 is zero, move this part as detached. If it is $7F, go directly to axe deflection.
Low byte of the absolute indexed operand at $3B18. X receives the signed Y displacement selected by the caller's index into $24D6.
Read the parent actor pointer from child fields 13 and 14. Copy parent X minus $0C and parent Y plus the displacement selected at $3B18, then apply the common adjustment and axe deflection.
Compute the part's rightward X offset and its vertical offset from the primary actor during the active phase. Branch to the special boss state path on phase zero and test axe deflection at the end.
Enter the left-side boss-part update with displacement index two.
Enter the right-side boss-part update with displacement index three.
Enter the left-side boss-part update with displacement index four.
Enter the right-side boss-part update with displacement index five.

Fourteen small values carried in the game image between the last attached-part entry and the detached-part routine. The entries at $3B8B and $3B9E take independent paths, and the active attached-part offsets come from $24D6. The values here have no identified consumer.
Advance X right and Y up by two for a detached part until Y drops below $0A, then clear the actor. Area bit $40 selects the replacement type $34 instead.
Copy four entries each from $3BE2 and $3BE6 to the actor shape table at $BEAE and the boss animation table.
Four sprite pointers copied to $BEAE–$BEB1 by $3BD0.
Four sprite pointers copied into the boss animation table by $3BD0.
The two four-entry boss sprite pointer tables end before this address. The following 22 bytes through $3BFF are zero in both hand-over and play.
Copy $97 and $96 into the live operands at $0D57 and $0D62, determining the VIC memory selection and first background value in a later IRQ.
Turn off play updates, seed music and background state and clear the top-left and vitality display fields. Continue into HUD setup.
Save A to $0653 and clear the patched operand at $0E70.
Seed $4B with $3F and return X equal to $15.
Save A to $0646, clear the axe flag at $0631 and redraw the equipment icon.
Run $1EC9 to prepare the round, then clear $72.
Disable all sprites and tail-call the 100-tick wait.
Blank the score cells and write two zero digits. For the second player path, clear its cells as well before updating the common cells and calling $0CBE.
Write A to the sprite X high-bit register and enable the display with raster compare bit 8 clear.
Disable sprites, set $70 to $20 for the banner, wait 100 ticks, and store the returned zero in the banner gate.
Test the F7 matrix bit, set $0661 while paused, and wait for release before accepting another press. The quit path sets $8F and clears $84 before leaving pause.
Immediate port value restored at pause exit. The entry at $3D00 saves the caller's CIA1 port A byte here.
Use nested delay loops and poll the F7 matrix row until released. Restore X and Y from self-modified immediate operands.
Saved X register operand of the LDX after the key-release scan. The adjacent LDY restores the Y value patched at $3D6F.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $3D6E. The pause wait stores the caller's Y here and reloads it on leaving the loop.
Set $8F, clear $84 and continue to the common pause exit that clears $0661.
Request sound $18, set $71 and $7C and position the player at world X=$10E0. Replace the two scroll JSR opcodes with absolute LDA opcodes before leaving pause.
Restore the JSR opcodes at $0DD0 and $0DD8, clear the playfield, and select the round character tail for the next playfield raster pass.
Save A as $0652, clear the current round and saved round fields, select the first area mask, initialize the HUD state, and open the banner gate.
Immediate starting-round value. The path at $3E20 restores zero here before player selection.
Immediate operand shared by the area-bit and player state stores. The reset path at $3E20 restores this byte to one.
Patch the starting round immediate to zero and the starting area immediate to one before returning to player selection.

Temporarily replace $30A8 with RTS, read the byte at $30A0 into A, and restore the LDY opcode at $30A8. Load the axe state before entering the 100-tick wait. The VICE instruction trace reached the sequence from the round setup.
Set the raster display to the fixed glyph set, disable fine horizontal scrolling and set background colors 0, 6 and 4 before drawing the round bonus panel.
Write outcome $0B if $85 is nonzero or $71 is zero.
VIC sprite shape selections for the screen at $4000. Both banner and actor rendering overwrite these bytes during raster processing.
VIC pointers $10 through $1F. Includes title animation cells starting at $10 and the second title sprite at $1F.
VIC pointers $20 through $2F. This group contains object silhouettes and repeats of terrain or obstacle shapes.
VIC pointers $30 through $3F. This group includes small creature and round object poses.
VIC pointers $40 through $4F. The contact sheet shows creature silhouettes and small collectible shapes.
VIC pointers $50 through $5F. This group contains thin projectiles and alternating walking creature poses.
VIC pointers $60 through $6F. Includes the player pose used by the bonus screen at pointer $6F.
VIC pointers $70 through $7F. A mixture of player poses, sprites with board-like silhouettes and bonus graphics.
VIC pointers $80 through $8F. The large display letters in this group include A through U with gaps.
VIC pointers $90 through $9F. The first cells include large banner digits followed by object shapes.
VIC pointers $A0 through $AF. Includes large creature silhouettes assembled from separate hardware cells.
VIC pointers $B0 through $BB. The contact sheet shows large shape fragments and cells with sparse pixel rows.
The prepare-round loop writes all 256 zero-page bytes here before the round starts.
Eight bytes per glyph. Screen codes below $80 include the vitality bar shapes, player and high-score logos, and the letters and numbers used by the title prompts.
Eight bytes per glyph for codes $80–$FF. These character cells include icon and pattern pieces used by the panel renderer.
First three glyphs in the round character set. The round-specific unpacker begins at the fourth glyph at $7818.
Playfield row 1 in the forest round. The word prefix is 15, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $25 $25 $25 $25 $25 $25.
Playfield row 2 in the forest round. The word prefix is 14, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $21 $21 $21 $21 $21 $21.
Playfield row 3 in the forest round. The word prefix is 17, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $1F $1F $1F $1F $1F $1F.
Playfield row 4 in the forest round. The word prefix is 199, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $20 $20 $20 $46 $12 $16.
Playfield row 5 in the forest round. The word prefix is 191, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $20 $20 $20 $46 $12 $16.
Playfield row 6 in the forest round. The word prefix is 210, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $20 $20 $20 $46 $12 $16.
Playfield row 7 in the forest round. The word prefix is 218, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $20 $20 $20 $15 $12 $14.
Playfield row 8 in the forest round. The word prefix is 222, followed by the row stream. Its first six cell codes are $20 $20 $20 $15 $12 $14.
